title: B-Cell Neoplasm Markers: t(14;18), IGHV, BRAF V600E and MYD88
summary: Learn the molecular fingerprints of follicular lymphoma, CLL, hairy cell leukemia and Waldenström macroglobulinemia, why a t(14;18) PCR can miss, and how to read IGHV and TP53 results in CLL.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 77 Hits 7 (t(14;18) in follicular lymphoma and PCR detection), 8 (CLL TP53 and IGHV), 9 (hairy cell leukemia BRAF V600E) and 11 (MYD88 L265P and CXCR4 in LPL/WM), and Exam Traps 1 (negative t(14;18) PCR) and 3 (unmutated IGHV is not favorable). Checked against Panjan 2023, Selvi 2012, ERIC IGHV recommendations 2022 and 2024, ERIC TP53 recommendations 2018, Tiacci 2011 (read via a page-fetch tool), Falini 2022, Ahmadzadeh 2014, Yan 2024 and Shin 2016. Three qualifications are recorded: PCR detection of t(14;18) depends on primer coverage (rv-ch77-t1418-pcr-coverage); the IGHV cut-off has a borderline zone and subset #2 exception (rv-ch77-ighv-borderline); MYD88 L265P detection is method-dependent and the variant is not exclusive to WM (rv-ch77-myd88-not-exclusive). The reviewer’s germinal-centre explanation for mutated IGHV was not checked against a source read and is not taught. Not taught: specific treatment regimens.

objectives: State the hallmark molecular lesion of follicular lymphoma, hairy cell leukemia and Waldenström macroglobulinemia, with approximate frequencies.
Explain why a t(14;18) PCR can be negative in follicular lymphoma and when FISH is preferred.
Interpret an IGHV identity result and TP53 testing in CLL.
Recognise that MYD88 L265P supports but does not by itself prove Waldenström macroglobulinemia.

scenes.title: Three B-cell reports
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three molecular reports on B-cell neoplasms arrive together — (1) a lymph node with the morphology and immunophenotype of follicular lymphoma; t(14;18) PCR (major breakpoint region primers only): negative; (2) a CLL patient’s IGHV report: 99.1% identity to germline; (3) an older adult with an IgM paraprotein and marrow lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate: MYD88 L265P detected. Question token: “Ruled out, favorable, proven?”

cues.text: Three B-cell reports arrive. A lymph node that looks like follicular lymphoma has a negative t(14;18) PCR.
A CLL report says the IGHV gene is 99.1 percent identical to germline.
And a patient with an IgM paraprotein carries MYD88 L265P. Is the lymphoma ruled out, is the CLL favorable, and is the third diagnosis proven?

scenes.title: Four molecular fingerprints
scenes.altText: Four cards. Follicular lymphoma: t(14;18)(q32;q21) joins BCL2 to the IGH locus, over-expressing the anti-apoptotic BCL2 protein; present in up to about 90% of cases (more than 80% in another series), and not limited to follicular lymphoma. CLL: the somatic hypermutation status of the clonal IGHV gene, reported as % identity to germline; a stable biomarker. Hairy cell leukemia: BRAF V600E, found in every case tested in the discovery study and in none of nearly 200 other peripheral B-cell lymphomas and leukemias; constitutively activates the MAPK pathway and is a drug target. Waldenström macroglobulinemia: MYD88 mutation (almost always L265P) in about 93–97% in Western series (87.8% in a large Chinese cohort); CXCR4 mutations in about 30–40%.

cues.text: Each of these B-cell neoplasms has a molecular fingerprint. In follicular lymphoma, the t(14;18) translocation moves BCL2 next to the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus, so the cell over-makes an anti-apoptotic protein. It is found in up to about ninety percent of cases.
In CLL, the key test is the mutation status of the IGHV gene, reported as percent identity to the germline sequence. Unlike acquired genomic lesions, it stays stable over time.

In hairy cell leukemia, the hallmark is BRAF V600E. In the discovery study it was in every hairy cell case tested and in none of nearly two hundred other B-cell lymphomas and leukemias. It switches on the MAPK pathway, and BRAF inhibitors target it.
In Waldenström macroglobulinemia, MYD88 mutations, almost all L265P, are found in about ninety-three to ninety-seven percent of cases in Western series, and CXCR4 mutations in about a third.

scenes.title: Why a t(14;18) PCR can miss
scenes.altText: Schematic of the chromosome 18 side of t(14;18): an arrow labelled “BCL2 3′ region” with breakpoint clusters as tokens — MBR (major breakpoint region, about 150 bp in the 3′ untranslated part of exon 3): 50–65% of breakpoints; 3′MBR and intermediate cluster region: some; mcr (minor cluster region, about 20 kb downstream): 10–20%. On chromosome 14 the break is almost always in a JH segment. Method cards: PCR — primers cover only short segments, sensitivity about 60–70% (up to about 88% with multiple primer sets), but shows the exact breakpoint and can track minimal residual disease; FISH — probes cover the whole IGH and BCL2 genes, sensitivity close to 100%.

cues.text: Why does PCR miss? On chromosome 14 the break almost always falls in a joining segment. On chromosome 18 it is scattered. The major breakpoint region, a stretch of about one hundred fifty base pairs, holds about fifty to sixty-five percent of breakpoints.
The minor cluster region, about twenty kilobases away, holds ten to twenty percent, and others fall in between. A primer pair only amplifies the short segment it was designed for.

So PCR detects the translocation in only about sixty to seventy percent of cases, rising to about eighty-eight percent with several primer sets. Its strengths are the exact breakpoint and minimal residual disease tracking.
FISH probes cover the whole IGH and BCL2 genes, so they catch breaks almost anywhere, with sensitivity close to one hundred percent. A negative PCR does not rule out follicular lymphoma.

scenes.title: Reading the CLL report
scenes.altText: IGHV card (ERIC 2022): % identity to germline, to two decimals: ≥98% = unmutated (U-CLL), generally adverse, poor response to chemoimmunotherapy and shorter progression-free survival after fixed-duration venetoclax plus anti-CD20 (ERIC 2024); <98% = mutated (M-CLL); 97–97.99% = borderline, interpret with caution; stereotyped subset #2 is adverse regardless of mutation status. TP53 card (ERIC 2018): del(17p) by FISH and TP53 mutation by sequencing (about 5% of untreated patients have a TP53 mutation without del(17p)); both predict chemoimmunotherapy resistance; targeted agents (BCR-signalling and BCL2 inhibitors) work in these patients; test before every line of treatment; by NGS report variants above 10% VAF. Hook answers card.

cues.text: Read the IGHV report as percent identity to germline. Ninety-eight percent or more is unmutated CLL, the adverse group, with poor response to chemoimmunotherapy. Below ninety-eight percent is mutated CLL, the more indolent group.
Two cautions: ninety-seven to ninety-seven point nine nine percent is borderline, and stereotyped subset two is adverse whatever its mutation status.

TP53 is the other key marker. Deletion 17p is found by FISH, but some patients have a TP53 mutation without the deletion, so sequencing is needed too, before every line of treatment. These patients resist chemoimmunotherapy but respond to targeted agents.
Back to the hook: the negative PCR does not exclude follicular lymphoma, and FISH is the more sensitive test. And 99.1 percent identity is unmutated: the adverse result.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “A negative t(14;18) PCR rules out follicular lymphoma” (✓ PCR misses breakpoints outside its primers; morphology and immunophenotype make the diagnosis, FISH is more sensitive); “Unmutated IGHV is the favorable kind” (✓ unmutated = ≥98% identity = adverse); “MYD88 L265P proves Waldenström” (✓ also in IgM MGUS and about 30% of ABC-type diffuse large B-cell lymphoma; low-sensitivity methods such as Sanger miss many cases).

cues.text: Trap one: a negative t(14;18) PCR rules out follicular lymphoma. No: PCR misses breakpoints outside its primers. Morphology and immunophenotype make the diagnosis, and FISH is more sensitive.
Trap two: unmutated IGHV is the favorable kind because mutations sound bad. No: unmutated, ninety-eight percent or more identical, is the adverse group.
Trap three: MYD88 L265P proves Waldenström macroglobulinemia. No: it is also found in IgM MGUS and in some diffuse large B-cell lymphomas. It supports the diagnosis in context.

scenes.title: Flashlight, photocopy, hallmark
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “PCR is a FLASHLIGHT on one spot of BCL2; FISH lights the whole ROOM. An IGHV that is a near-perfect PHOTOCOPY of germline (≥98%) is the dangerous one. BRAF is the HAIRY cell’s hallmark; MYD88 is the IgM clue, not the verdict.” Tokens: flashlight = PCR · photocopy = unmutated · hallmark = BRAF. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: PCR is a flashlight on one spot of BCL2, while FISH lights the whole room. An IGHV gene that is a near-perfect photocopy of germline is the dangerous one. BRAF is the hairy cell hallmark, and MYD88 is the IgM clue, not the verdict.

Where it breaks: several primer sets make PCR far better than one flashlight; borderline identity and subset two do not follow the photocopy rule; with BTK inhibitors the IGHV difference in progression-free survival may disappear; and rare hairy cell cases lack V600E.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “t(14;18) PCR negative ≠ no follicular lymphoma · IGHV ≥98% identity = unmutated = adverse”, “BRAF V600E = hairy cell · MYD88 L265P supports, does not prove, Waldenström”.

cues.text: A negative t(14;18) PCR does not rule out follicular lymphoma, unmutated IGHV (at least 98% identical to germline) is the adverse CLL result, BRAF V600E marks hairy cell leukemia, and MYD88 L265P supports but does not prove Waldenström macroglobulinemia.

props.label: PCR − ≠ no FL · IGHV ≥ 98% identity = unmutated = adverse
BRAF V600E = hairy cell · MYD88 L265P supports WM

explanation.what: Plain language: many B-cell cancers carry a typical genetic change that helps name them. Follicular lymphoma usually has a swap between chromosomes 14 and 18; hairy cell leukemia almost always has one BRAF change; Waldenström macroglobulinemia usually has one MYD88 change; and in CLL, how much the antibody gene has changed from its inherited version predicts how the disease behaves. Scientific terms: t(14;18)(q32;q21), IGH-BCL2, major breakpoint region (MBR), minor cluster region (mcr), FISH, IGHV somatic hypermutation (SHM), % germline identity, U-CLL and M-CLL, stereotyped subset #2, del(17p), TP53, variant allele frequency (VAF), BRAF V600E, MAPK pathway, MYD88 L265P, CXCR4, allele-specific PCR (AS-PCR), droplet digital PCR (ddPCR).
explanation.why: The t(14;18) puts BCL2 under the control of the IGH locus so the cell over-expresses an anti-apoptotic protein. Chromosome 18 breakpoints are scattered across several clusters, so a primer pair covering one cluster misses the others, whereas FISH probes span the whole genes. In CLL, an IGHV sequence close to germline marks a clinically more aggressive disease; TP53 loss causes chemoimmunotherapy resistance. BRAF V600E constitutively activates MAPK signalling in hairy cell leukemia.
explanation.measure: Follicular lymphoma: t(14;18) in up to about 90%; MBR 50–65% and mcr 10–20% of breakpoints; PCR sensitivity about 60–70% (up to about 88% with several primer sets), FISH close to 100%. CLL: ≥98% identity = unmutated, <98% = mutated, 97–97.99% = borderline; del(17p) by FISH plus TP53 sequencing before every line of treatment, NGS variants reported above 10% VAF. HCL: BRAF V600E in every case tested in the discovery study and in none of nearly 200 other B-cell neoplasms. WM: MYD88 mutation (almost always L265P) about 93–97% in Western series (87.8% in a Chinese cohort); CXCR4 about 30–40%.
explanation.differs: PCR (exact breakpoint, MRD, misses some breakpoints) vs FISH (near-complete detection); unmutated (≥98% identity, adverse) vs mutated IGHV (<98%, more indolent); classic HCL (BRAF V600E) vs HCL-variant (BRAF V600E not detected); WM (MYD88 L265P in most) vs IgM MGUS and ABC-type DLBCL (can also carry it).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: which translocation or mutation matches which neoplasm, what a negative t(14;18) PCR means, which IGHV result is adverse, and whether MYD88 L265P alone proves Waldenström macroglobulinemia.

questions.stem: A lymph node has the morphology and immunophenotype of follicular lymphoma, but a t(14;18) PCR using major breakpoint region primers is negative. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: Follicular lymphoma is not excluded; FISH for IGH-BCL2 is more sensitive
options.rationale: Correct. PCR primers cover only short DNA segments, so sensitivity is only about 60–70%, whereas FISH probes span the whole IGH and BCL2 genes and detect breaks across BCL2.
Incorrect. PCR sensitivity is only about 60–70%, and morphology and immunophenotype make the diagnosis.

options.text: The result proves a minor cluster region breakpoint
options.rationale: Incorrect. A negative MBR PCR cannot locate the breakpoint; the case may also lack the translocation.

options.text: Repeat the same PCR on peripheral blood to confirm
options.rationale: Incorrect. The same primers would miss the same breakpoint; a method with wider coverage is needed.

questions.stem: A CLL IGHV sequencing report gives 99.1% identity to the closest germline gene; the case is not a stereotyped subset. How is it classified?

options.text: Unmutated IGHV, the adverse prognostic group
options.rationale: Correct. ERIC classifies ≥98% germline identity as unmutated CLL, associated with adverse prognosis and poor response to chemoimmunotherapy.

options.text: Mutated IGHV, the favorable prognostic group
options.rationale: Incorrect. Mutated CLL is below 98% identity; this sequence is almost germline.

options.text: Not interpretable without a TP53 result
options.rationale: Incorrect. IGHV status is assigned on its own; TP53 is a separate, additional marker.

questions.stem: A patient with an IgM paraprotein has MYD88 L265P detected in bone marrow by allele-specific PCR. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It supports lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma/Waldenström macroglobulinemia but also occurs in IgM MGUS and some diffuse large B-cell lymphomas
options.rationale: Correct. MYD88 L265P is found in most WM, but also in IgM MGUS and about 30% of ABC-type DLBCL, so it is read with morphology and clinical findings.

options.text: It proves Waldenström macroglobulinemia on its own
options.rationale: Incorrect. The variant is not exclusive to WM.

options.text: A negative Sanger result would have excluded Waldenström macroglobulinemia
options.rationale: Incorrect. Sanger sequencing detected the variant in only about 61% of WM in one large cohort, far fewer than AS-PCR.

options.text: BRAF V600E is expected in the same clone
options.rationale: Incorrect. BRAF V600E is the hallmark of hairy cell leukemia and was not found in other B-cell neoplasms in the discovery study.

claims.text: t(14;18) joins BCL2 to IGH, over-expressing anti-apoptotic BCL2; up to ~90% of FL; not limited to FL.
Breakpoint clusters (MBR ~150 bp, 50–65%; mcr 10–20%); PCR ~60–70% (up to ~88% multi-primer); FISH close to 100%; PCR gives exact breakpoint and MRD.
IGHV ≥98% identity unmutated (adverse), <98% mutated, 97–97.99% borderline; subset #2 adverse; stable biomarker; BTK-inhibitor follow-up shows no PFS gap.
Reviewer: mutated IGHV means the B cell matured through the germinal centre.
claims.note: Not checked against a source read in this session; not taught.

claims.text: del(17p)/TP53 mutation: chemoimmunotherapy resistance; targeted agents effective; ~5% mutation without deletion; test before every line; NGS >10% VAF.
BRAF V600E in every HCL tested in the discovery study, none of nearly 200 other B-cell neoplasms; MAPK activation; BRAF inhibitors; absent in HCL-variant; rare V600E-negative HCL.
MYD88 L265P ~93–97% WM (87.8% Chinese cohort), method-dependent detection; CXCR4 ~30–40%; also in IgM MGUS and ~30% ABC DLBCL.

accuracyFlags.issue: Reviewer Ch. 77 Hit 7 and Trap 1 attribute the 60–70% PCR detection rate to 30–40% of breakpoints falling outside the MBR. Panjan 2023 gives the MBR as 50–65% and the mcr as 10–20% of breakpoints, with PCR sensitivity of 60–70% that rises to about 88% with multiple primer sets, and FISH close to 100%. The detection rate therefore depends on how many breakpoint regions the primer sets cover; the lesson teaches it as method-dependent.

Reviewer Ch. 77 Hit 8 gives the IGHV cut-off (unmutated ≤2% divergence) and says high risk “needs BTK/BCL2 inhibitors”. ERIC 2022 confirms the 98% identity cut-off but adds a 97–97.99% borderline group to interpret with caution and states stereotyped subset #2 is adverse regardless of mutation status; longer follow-up of BTK-inhibitor trials showed no PFS difference between mutated and unmutated CLL. The lesson adds this context and does not teach a treatment rule.

Reviewer Ch. 77 Hit 11 gives MYD88 L265P in >90% of LPL/WM. Yan 2024 cites MYD88 mutation (almost always L265P) in about 93–97% of WM in Western series but found 87.8% in 385 Chinese patients, with detection strongly method-dependent (Sanger 61.4%, NGS 74.4%, AS-PCR 84.2%, ddPCR 79.0%); Shin 2016 notes MYD88 L265P in IgM MGUS (up to 87%) and about 30% of ABC-type DLBCL, so it is not an exclusive marker. The lesson teaches MYD88 L265P as supportive, not diagnostic on its own.
